## D279 — R7.3a batch 2 (kernel), part 2: the live per-module error classes folded into module refusals (2026-10-24)

**Scope** (option 4(a), narrowed by reachability; the coordinator agreed).
- Only 117 of cad's 401 source files are reachable by imports from the live engine: `src/part/part-model.ts`, `src/api`
  and `src/io`. The other **284 files** are reachable only through `index.ts` exports: createCadModel, the old
  document versions, the native "proof" APIs (convex-planar-*, xy-affine-*, translated-strip, paired, exact-proof, the
  wide-curve operations). They hold 141 of the 171 error classes. That count is the size of R7.3d's audit: each module
  there retires (and its class with it) or stays, and a kept one is folded then.
- Of the 30 live classes, 8 stay named classes, because something outside the live engine tells them apart by class:
  - CadPartError, BrepError, FitError, IGESImportError, SubdError, SurfaceIntersectionError (cad-model and the studio);
  - HullError (cad-model);
  - NativeCurvatureError and NativeSecondDerivativeError (examples/cad-nurbs' demos and cad-interop's examples check
    `instanceof` and `name`);
  - CadAstError (a structured diagnostic, with its range and object, returned by compileCadModel).
- The other **21 are folded**: BearingError, CamError, ConnectorError, CurvedArrangementError, DriveError,
  DxfWriteError, ExtrudedProfileError, FacetBooleanError, FlatPatternError, FrameSectionError, GearError, GlandError,
  MeshBrepError, PlanarArrangementError, PrismaticSolidError, SewError, ShaftError, ShaftPartError, SheetMetalError,
  SolidMassError, SpringError.

**The fold.**
- `src/core/barocss-error.ts`:
  - `kernelRefusal(source, code, message, cause?)`: a KernelError named `BarocssError`, its code, its message as the
    module writes it, `details.source` naming the module;
  - `isFrom(e, source)`.
- Each folded class becomes a factory and a guard in its module:
  `gearError(code, detail)` (the same message the class wrote, e.g. `gear: …`) and `isGearError(e)`. The guard is what
  the 46 catch sites that told modules apart by class use now: the part model mapping a gear's codes, the facet Boolean
  catching the mesh builder, and so on. Codes of two modules share names (INPUT …), so `source`, not the code, says
  whose a refusal is.
- The main entry exports the factories and guards in place of the classes. No message text changes, and every code is
  as before.
- The folded errors' `name` is `BarocssError`. The fingerprint records only the part model's refusals, which are
  CadPartErrors, so it does not move.
- Legacy `modeling.ts` told the extruded profile's refusal by its class name, so as not to import the profile builder
  (its tests' bundle traps forbid it). It now tells it by `isFrom(…, 'extruded-profile')`.
- `test/error-codes.test.mjs` also reads each `kernelRefusal(…) as … { code: C }` factory's C, so the folded modules'
  codes stay in `CAD_ERROR_CODES`.

**Tests:** `assert.throws(…, XError)` and `instanceof XError` in the kernel's tests became the guards; nothing else in
them changed.

**Checks** (in a scratch worktree at 553edb8a8 + the change):
- cad tsc and eslint clean.
- Kernel suite at concurrency 4: 1725/1732, 6 skipped, the one failure the native-split demo's Node-version assertion.
  Names identical to part 1's run.
- R5 fingerprint byte-identical: 869 cases `49f1fac8…`. RB: no NEW, the same 2 TODOs.
- cad-model 1089/1089, studio 286/286, the docs samples 36/36.
- At the commit's parent 88deb6df7 the samples are 47/48. The failing one, cad-model-api's "rows from a person's file,
  then a fastener from them", fails on that tip without this change too: not this change's.
- No refusal text changed: the docs table stays. No flow: nothing studio-visible.

**Where the change is in history:** the fold's code (69 files under `packages/barocss-cad`) is in `44cb23283`, the
coordinator's roadmap commit. The patch was applied in the shared integration worktree for its last check, and that
commit took the working tree with it. The patch and the commit's cad diff are identical. `a152dee7e` holds this record
and the README row. Integration is never rewritten, so the two stay as they are; read them together as D279.

## D280 — R7.3b (kernel): results as data, mass in MMGS (2026-10-24)

**On branch `claude/kernel-r73b-r77b`**, the coordinator's one merge window, with R7.7b next on the same branch; the
outer, API and docs lanes branch from it. Design: `notes/r73b-r77b` in the shared notes, approved.

**Mass in MMGS** (api-conventions §2).
- `MassProperties` (was `SolidMassProperties`) is `{ volume mm³, mass g, centroid mm, inertia g·mm² about the centroid,
  method, volumeBound? }`. A density is in g/cm³:
  - `mass = ρ · V · 1e-3`;
  - inertia = `ρ · 1e-3 ·` the second moments in mm⁵.
- Live everywhere: `brepMassProperties`, `prismaticMassProperties`, `solidMassFromIntegrals`, `combineMassProperties`
  (parallel axes in mm and g), `revolveMassProperties`, loft, the part model's hollowed and moved masses.
- The cut list: `CutPiece.density`, a row's `mass` and `totalMass`, `totals.mass` in g, `cutList(pieces, { density })`,
  `cutPiece(output, { volume? })`. The CSV still shows kg, a person's unit for a cut list.
- The legacy createCadModel surface keeps its own kg types until R7.3d.

**Results as data** (§4).
- `CadPartOutput` and `CadPartSnapshot` have no methods. The new functions are on the main entry:

  | Was | Now |
  |---|---|
  | `o.massProperties(ρ kg/m³)` | `massPropertiesOf(o, ρ g/cm³ = 1)` |
  | `o.surfaceArea()` | `surfaceAreaOf(o)` |
  | `o.validate()` | `checkOutput(o)` |
  | `o.exportStl(options)` | `exportStl(o, options)` |
  | `o.exportStep(options)` | `exportStep(o, options)` (exportStep also takes B-reps, as before) |
  | `o.flatPattern(options)` | `flatPatternOf(o, options)` |
  | `s.output(id)` | `outputOf(s, id)` |
  | `s.withParameters(e)` | `reevaluate(s, { parameters: e })` |
  | `s.withDocument(d)` | `reevaluate(s, { document: d })` |
  | `s.save()` | `saveCadPart(s)` |

- What a function needs beyond the data (the part an output was made from, its cached validation, area and flats; a
  snapshot's cache and options) is in module WeakMaps. An output made elsewhere falls back to its B-rep.

**Call sites.**
- The kernel's tests and scripts were rewritten by a TS-checker codemod, which changed only receivers typed
  CadPartOutput, CadPartSnapshot or MassProperties, and untyped ones in files that do not use the legacy API.
- Where a unit made the oracle's numbers move, the oracle's factors went to g, the formulas kept: frk3-oracle, fr-s0,
  frk-4-revolve, shared-seam, mass-polyhedral, sweep-mass-overlap, freeform, the part model's box inertia, fr-4a's cut
  list.
- conformance/fr's four cut-list cases expect `density` 7.85 and masses in g: the same closed forms (ρ·A·L), in g.
- Densities given as numbers in tests went ÷1000, with 1 kept as the volume-only density.

  conversions; their result shapes are theirs (R7.7d).

`49f1fac8…`).
- Every body's mass record changed, and nothing else did: refusals, F/E/V, areas, validity and meshes are

## D281 — Coplanar pieces apart keep their own names (2026-10-28)

**Owner, 2026-10-28**: join coplanar pieces only where they meet; faces apart keep their own names ("이름이 바뀌는 것은
허용": names may change).

**Before.** The analytic Boolean's `mergePieces` joined every kept piece on one plane (or cylinder) facing one way into a
single union, and every resulting face took the first piece's name. A row of bosses on a rounded plate had all its top
faces renamed after one boss at every Boolean (`c3.top#1` … `#4` after the fourth), so a reference to an earlier boss's
top moved with each new boss; and the union of all of them was rebuilt at every step.

**Now.** Pieces of a coplanar group are clustered by their domain boxes (padded by 10 tolerances, meeting directly or
through others). A cluster is joined (`booleanCurveRegions`, as before) and each face it makes takes the name of the first
piece lying in it; a piece alone whose rings close is passed through as it is, with its own name. A row of bosses keeps
`c0.top`, `c1.top`, ….

**What changed in the records.**
- Shapes: validity, bodies, faces, edges, vertices, volume and centroid identical on every bench case.
- Kernel: `r12-s0` (the tray's `fe3.side1` … now their own), three R12 conformance cases' `faceNames` (names added, none
  lost: `c.start`, `fl.leg.outer`, `c1.side1`, `f1.tip` …), the flat-DXF fixtures re-written with the oracle (the
  outline's coordinates moved in the last digit: 1e-14).
- Model: `o7-legacy/expected.json`, one message: the enclosure's CNC corner check counts sharp edges by their two
  faces' names, and 8 edges that had been counted as 4 pairs (their faces shared a renamed name) are now 8. That one line
  only; the rest of the oracle is unchanged.

**Checks.** Kernel suite: the 28 baseline failures only. Model suite (1711): the two baseline solver failures only (D240's
timing assertion failed once under load and passes alone).

## D282 — Half circles stay whole at rounding; repeated face names keep their order; incremental stitch not landed (2026-10-28)

**Owner, 2026-10-28**: find why the full rebuild makes one more vertex than the incremental stitch, make the two give
the same topology, then apply the incremental stitch.

**Cause of the extra vertex.** The curved arrangement splits an arc over half a turn in two (`halves`), so no piece
starts and ends at one vertex. It split at exactly `|sweep| > π`. A boss's half circle on a rounded plate's top is read
back from the stitched edge at every Boolean, and its sweep drifts in the last bits: after the sixth boss it came out
−3.141592653589794, one ulp past π, and was split at its top (10, 11, 8). That vertex split the neighbouring cylinder's
edge (`c0.side0#1|p.top` → `#1`, `#2`): one more edge and vertex on an edge no cut touched. The incremental stitch kept
the face's input edge and never re-read it. **Fix**: `halves` splits only past π + 1e-12, the margin `simplify` already
keeps arcs within.

**A second fault found on the way.** Faces of one name (a cylinder's two halves, `c0.side0#1`, `#2`) are numbered by
their points inside, compared exactly. The two halves' points have one x to within rounding (10 ± 4e-15), so the order
was decided by the last bits and flipped from one Boolean to the next: in a row of bosses the first boss's lower half
was `c0.side0#1` after b0, `#2` after b1, `#1` after b2. A reference to it changed meaning as later bosses were added.
**Fix**: a coordinate within 100 tolerances counts as equal and the next decides (`keyOrder`); the name now stays at
every step.

**The incremental stitch, measured again.** With both fixes, the patch (far faces' loops and edges taken from the
input, put in first) gives the full rebuild's topology on every bench case (counts, volume, centroid) and −13 % on the
rounded plate + 48 bosses. But it puts edges and vertices in another order and at the input's points, not the rebuilt
ones: a test that picks "the first straight edge at z = 10" (R10.1) got another edge, and byte-frozen outputs (flat DXF,
drawing-table DXF, robot URDF/SDF/USD) changed in the last digits. Made to follow the full rebuild exactly — every
piece through the vertex merge, the T-junction split and the edge search, only the edges a frozen face leaves whole
taking their input curves, and frozen faces their input surfaces — it gives the same records as the rebuild at every
step of the 12-boss chain, and **no gain** (48 bosses 514 → 518 ms, within noise): the time the patch saved was those
steps. So it is not landed; the faster, order-changing version stays as
`notes/patches/incremental-stitch-frozen-faces-2026-10-28.patch`. A real gain needs the stitch's per-step
work (vertex merge, T-junction search, `checkBrep`, ~70 % of it) done only around the faces that changed, which changes
what is compared, not only how fast.

**Records.**
- Shapes: the rounded-plate chains lose the spurious edge and vertex (12 bosses: 88 → 87 edges, 59 → 58 vertices; 24
  and 48 bosses the same). Every other bench case: validity, counts, volume and centroid unchanged.
- Names: repeated face names keep their numbering across Booleans where it flipped by rounding. One conformance case
  names a face that had been numbered by rounding: the oblique groove's two top faces (`pe.top#1`, `#2`, one each side of
  the groove, points inside at one x) swapped, the lower y now `#1`. Its input now names the same rim
  (`c0.side0|pe.top#2#1`); its expected record is unchanged.
- New test `boolean-boss-row.test.mjs`: 8 bosses on a rounded plate add 6 edges and 4 vertices each and the first boss's
  `c0.side0#1` stays one half (fails on the old build at b1).
- Checks: kernel suite (1958, before the new test, which passes alone): the 28 baseline failures only, plus the groove
  case before its rename; model suite 1711: the two baseline solver failures
  only. Bench: shapes unchanged except the rounded-plate chains above.

**Also.** `scripts/code-shape.mjs` no longer counts a for-of's iterable or a for's initializer as inside the loop (they
are evaluated once); the baseline is re-recorded lower (loop-spread 295 → 274, loop-literal 82 → 75).

## D283 — Incremental stitch: far faces keep their input loops; record order may change (2026-10-28)

**Owner, 2026-10-28**: apply the faster incremental stitch (D282's measured −13 %), accepting that edge and vertex
order and last-digit coordinates change; update the tests and frozen files that read them.

**Change.** In the analytic Boolean, a face kept whole and far from the other solid (no cut, 1000 tolerances clear of
its box; not a NURBS face through a pole) is *frozen*: the stitch takes its loops, edges, vertices and surface from its
input B-rep instead of rebuilding them, and puts its edges in first; neighbours find them as they find a copy of a
curve. A face is frozen only where its rebuilt boundary would be its input loops one for one (no curve dropped, halved
or fitted in pieces), so its edges are the ones the rebuild would make. Any `BrepError` rebuilds the whole as before.
D282's two fixes (arcs past π + 1e-12; repeated names ordered with a tolerance) are what make the topology the same.

**What changes and what does not.**
- Same: validity, bodies, faces, edges, vertices, volume and centroid on every bench case; edge names (as a set) at all
  13 steps of the rounded plate + 12 bosses. No fallback on the bench.
- Different: the order of edges and vertices in the B-rep, an edge's direction where the input's is kept, and the last
  digits of frozen faces' points (the input's, not re-derived).
- Time (median of 5, best of two rounds): rounded plate + 12 / 24 / 48 bosses −13 / −10 / −12 %; tilted boxes 48 −4 %;
  the rest within noise.

**Records updated.**
- `test/r10-1.test.mjs`: the rod-on-plate junction was picked as "the first straight edge at z = 10 with y > 0", which
  the plate's own edge at y = 20 also is; now y < 10 too (by where it lies, not its place in the list).
- Kernel `conformance/r12/flat-dxf/*`: re-written with the ezdxf oracle (`flat-dxf-fixtures.mjs`); coordinates move in
  the last digit (24.178318229274428 → …424).
- `conformance/r14/tables/bends`: the drawing-table DXF re-frozen (`UPDATE_DXF_FIXTURES`) and read again by ezdxf
  (`dxf-oracle.py`): the same 107 entities; 17 lines run the other way and the order differs.
- `conformance/rm/arm-6r`: `robot.sdf`, `robot.usda` (`UPDATE_USD_CASE`) and `robot.xml` (the same switch now also
  re-freezes the MJCF, `test/robot-sdf-usd.test.ts`): poses and inertia in the last digits (0.040000000000000015 →
  0.04), the USD mesh's triangulation. usd-core 26.8 read the new stage: its reading file is unchanged. MuJoCo 3.3.0
  re-run (`mjcf-oracle.py`, meshes from `cad-cli mjcf`): every check passes; static values move by ≤ 2e-15, the
  undamped 5 s hang's chaotic end values (`qvel_max` 74.5 → 56.2, `com_height_end`) by more. four-bar unchanged.
- `cad-model/test/fixtures/robot-frozen-boundary.json` (the frozen arm's byte pin, test `robot-frozen-mass`): its three
  non-inertial hashes and 54 refreshed inertia values re-pinned to the new files; the S0 `before` values unchanged.
- The patch file `notes/patches/incremental-stitch-frozen-faces-2026-10-28.patch` (D282) is removed: it is in the source now.
- Kept checked (2026-10-28): `test/incremental-stitch-differential.test.mjs` evaluates 15 chains (random rounded-plate
  boss/pocket rows, 12 bosses, two tilted-box rows) with the frozen path on and off (`stitchFreezing`, a module switch
  not exported from the package) and requires the same validity, counts, face and edge names, volume and centroid.

## D284 — Sketch results on the 1e-6 mm grid when the solver accepts them; a non-converging edit keeps its own reason (2026-10-28)

**Owner, 2026-10-28**: fix the studio sketch-solver mismatch — decide whether results snap to exact values and what a
conflict shows — and make `apps/cad-studio/test/constraints.test.ts` and the two cad-model solver tests pass.

**Before.** `d62571d69` (CAD review 2215, P0 "sketch output": preserve solver-approved coefficients, keep display
rounding separate, preserve the meaning of NONCONVERGENCE) removed `solveOutline`'s rounding of every solved point to
1e-6 mm and its mapping of NONCONVERGENCE to "These constraints conflict with each other or with the H/V edges". Its own
regressions (`sketch-profile-precision.test.ts`) were added; the older expectations were not updated. The kernel's
solver stops once every residual is within tolerance (1e-7 mm, 1e-9 rad), so results came back a few 1e-8 mm off:
a width of 60 as 59.999999964, a fixed-point neighbour as 36.0000000027. Seven of the studio test's 24 and both
cad-model solver tests failed on exact values, and a typed rectangle no longer read as a rectangle (`shapeNode`, the
QA S3/K29 case). Four studio tests expected the old "conflict" wording.

**Decision.**
1. *Snap only what the solver accepts.* After a successful solve, `solveOutline` rounds every solution point (outline
   points, arc centres, rule points) to the 1e-6 mm grid and solves again from them. If that solve succeeds without a
   step (`iterations === 0`: the kernel's own residual check passes on the snapped points as they are), the snapped
   solution is the result; otherwise the solver's values are kept. Ordinary designs in whole or short decimal mm come
   out exact; 2215's cases — an off-grid anchor, a driving 10.0000004, an off-grid circle centre — fail the check when
   snapped and stay as solved, so no accepted geometry is moved off its constraints. The cost is one extra solve that
   takes no step. The kernel is unchanged.
2. *A non-converging edit says only what the solver knows.* The studio keeps the kernel's diagnostic after the
   constraint's label ("Length of edge 3 = 50: XY numerical sketch: Bounded local solve did not meet fixed residual
   tolerances; this is not an inconsistency proof"), as 2215 requires: a local solve that does not converge has not
   proved the constraints contradict each other. The old wording claimed that.

**Records.** `packages/barocss-cad-model/src/sketch/profile.ts` (`solveOutline`, `snap`). `apps/cad-studio/test/
constraints.test.ts`: four expectations of "conflict" now expect the label and the solver's diagnostic (`NOT_SOLVED`),
because the old expectation was the wording 2215 withdrew; no numeric expectation was loosened. The two cad-model
solver tests (`engine.test.ts`) and `sketch-profile-precision.test.ts` pass unchanged. Docs:
`apps/library-docs/docs/how/sketch-solver.md`.

## D285 — The surface march refuses only what it cannot place; the new refusal codes listed (2026-10-28)

**Owner, 2026-10-28**: sort the 28 kernel failures kept as the baseline into causes, then fix them.

**Before.** `59a6c0201` ("refuse incomplete surface intersection chains") made `intersectPatches` throw where it had
ended a chain: a seed off a box by the 1e-9 slack, a bisection sample the corrector did not place, a step no halving
corrected. `36191ee28` (spring41c) recovered the first from 72 failures to 28. Of the 28: 22 were the same refusals
(R10.2–R10.4 fillets, the D97/R10.B steps, freeform tori and cones, five L4 fuzz cases), 1 the kernel's refusal-code
list missing 13 codes (`R7.3a`), 1 a Node version pinned by a demo, and 4 one L-plate case (below). Each geometric case
was checked against `59a6c0201^`'s marcher: all passed there, to their closed forms or oracles.

**Decision.**
1. *A curve that only passes a box's corner has no piece there.* A seed off the boxes whose every recovery step (both
   ways, down to 1/32 of a step) corrects onto the curve and lies outside is skipped, not refused (a boss's foot fillet
   wall at its upright edge, `[[u1, v1]]` of the wall's box). A recovery step that does not correct is refused as before.
2. *A failed correction in the bisection is neither inside nor outside.* The end is sought short of it (`hi = m`); the
   end kept is always a corrected inside point. Before a cone's apex or a ball's pole corrections fail within a few
   1e-6 of it, and D208/D269 carry the curve on to the point.
3. *No step corrected: the chain ends at its last point* (each point still checked on both surfaces), its loose end
   the stitch's to close or refuse (R10.4b's pipe tee, where the ball goes over onto the branch's rim). The budget, the
   per-direction step limit and the per-point check of `59a6c0201` stay.
4. *The refusal codes.* `CAD_REFUSAL_CODES` and `CAD_ERROR_CODES` gain the face fillet, face thread, full round and cone
   top chamfer codes. A `CadPartError` then carries the specific code (D278), so the face fillet's fallback to the
   rolling ball (`part-model.ts`) and three tests read the category from `details.category`. Docs refusal table
   regenerated.

**Left.** 4 of 28. The L-plate's six top edges (`r10-3a`, `conformance r10-corner-l-plate-top`, and `D101`, which
evaluates it): two convex rounds meet in a mitre whose two tool cylinders touch tangentially at a patch's edge, where
their two curves cross. The bisection hops between the branches and ends 4e-5 from the touch point; the stitch leaves
an edge used once. `59a6c0201^` ended it 7e-8 away because its march started 1e-14 elsewhere: both depend on the
rounding. A fix needs the end at a tangent touch found as such. And `native-split-reference-replay`: the demo it runs
asserts Node 22.23.3 (the recorded run's), this machine has 22.19.0; no kernel change.

**Records.** `packages/barocss-cad/src/intersect/surface-intersection.ts`, `src/core/error-codes.ts`,
`src/part/part-model.ts`; tests `face-fillet`, `face-thread`, `full-round`. Kernel 1961: 1951 pass, 4 fail (the four
above), none new; cad-model 1711/1711, studio 351/351.

## D286 — A chain ending at a tangent touch on a box's side ends at the touch; two more refusal codes listed (2026-10-28)

**Owner, 2026-10-28**: fix the L-plate mitre (D285's "left"): find the chain end at a tangent touch on a patch edge as
such, so the stitch joins it.

**Before.** An L-plate's six top edges rounded 2 (`r10-3a`, `conformance r10-corner-l-plate-top`, `D101`): at each outer
corner the two edges' tool cylinders (r 2, axes at z 8, square to each other) meet in two ellipses that cross at their
tops, (38, 18, 10) and its mirror, where the cylinders touch, tangent to the top face — on a side of one tool patch's
box. The march's step left the box there; the bisection's corrections landed on one ellipse or the other (n₁ × n₂ about
1e-6) and its end came 4e-5 from the touch. The stitch found an edge used once.

**Decision.** When the bisection's end has |n₁ × n₂| < 1e-3, the side of the box the step left by (of either patch) is
searched for the point nearest the other surface: golden section along that side, over the bisection's end and the
step's outside point widened by their distance either way, each sample projected onto the other surface. The point is
taken when it lies on both surfaces within the tolerance, inside the other patch's box (1e-9 slack) and no farther from
the end than the outside point; the chain's end tangent there is the step's own (the normals' cross has no direction).
Otherwise the bisection's end stands. Transversal ends (|n₁ × n₂| ≥ 1e-3) are unchanged, so no other result moved:
kernel names of passing tests the same before and after.

**Also.** `FilletRefusal`'s `RADIUS_EXCEEDS_CURVATURE` and `NOT_ANALYTIC_PAIR` are bracketed at run time (`[${code}]`)
and were missing from `CAD_REFUSAL_CODES`, so a refusal carried its category, not its code; the R7.3a test now also
reads the members of `*Refusal` string unions. `conformance/r10/refuse-radius-exceeds-curvature.json` expects the code
and the category as the other refusal cases do. The docs figure's formula box wraps (`white-space: normal`) instead of
scrolling: 70 of the How it works formulas were wider than the box.

**Records.** `packages/barocss-cad/src/intersect/surface-intersection.ts` (`touchOnSide`), `src/core/error-codes.ts`,
`test/error-codes.test.mjs`; `apps/library-docs/docs/.vitepress/components/algorithms/{AlgoFigure,FilletSection}.vue`.
Of D285's four left, the L-plate's three pass; `native-split-reference-replay` (a demo pinned to Node 22.23.3) remains.

## D287 — A whole turn of one cylinder's pieces is joined in two halves (2026-10-28)

**Owner, 2026-10-28**: after the corner restore, join the pieces of one cylinder and split them only at the seam, so
the face fillet's result matches the bare tee's.

**Before.** The analytic Boolean's `mergePieces` joins kept pieces on one plane or cylinder. For a cylinder it puts the
joined face's seam in the widest angle the pieces leave uncovered; when they cover the whole turn there is none, and
the pieces were kept as they were. The face fillet's corner restore (F1, `restoreCorner`: body − W) left the 60° tee's
main pipe in 8 pieces and the branch in 5 (the bare tee: 2 each), so the edge fillet after it ran on 20 faces (1.64 s
instead of 0.89 s) and the r 4 round across an r 2 one came out in 56 faces, not the bare tee's 45 (same volume).

**Decision.** A group of one cylinder's pieces covering the whole turn is cut at two seams half a turn apart — the
widest piece's start and its opposite — each piece in its own domain and only where a seam falls strictly inside its
span (10 tolerances in); the halves are joined as before, each with its seam in the half the other leaves. A piece no
seam crosses is kept as the same piece. When a cut leaves no region, the group stays as it was. Each half is named after
the first piece lying in it, as any join is.

**Results.** `tee60-over-round`: 45 faces, 124 edges, 82 vertices, the bare tee's r 4 round's face and edge names
exactly, volume to 12 digits, centroid 3e-13 apart; 6.1 → 5.2–5.4 s. `pin-face-fillet-over-round`: 27 faces as the
bare pin's, one edge more (71, 70), volume to 1e-10. The other 17 bench cases have the same shape (validity, counts,
names, volume, centroid); 7 of them differ in their bits. `conformance r10-translational-rod-across-disc`: the two
faces of R10.1's cap cylinder that lay on the plate's rim (`f_cyl.side0`, `f_cyl.side1`) are now pieces of the rim
`pe.side0`: its face names updated, volume and centroid as before. Kernel 1961: 1954 pass and the one above, its names updated, passes on its own (the rest skipped); cad-model 1711/1711,
studio 351/351.

**Records.** `packages/barocss-cad/src/brep/analytic-boolean.ts` (`joinPieces`, `seamHalves`);
`conformance/r10/translational-rod-across-disc.json`; `apps/library-docs/docs/how/naming.md` §4; research note §8.

## D288 — One polynomial B-spline guide reaches Studio Loft (2026-10-28)

**Result.** CG1.3's kernel WIP `bbc921cf7` now reaches Model/API, chat and the Studio Loft command. One copied
polynomial guide takes 2–8 ruled height sections. Degree is 1–5, with at most 64 controls, clamped knots and exactly
equal positive source weights. Controls must rise along the section normal. The guide must meet a vertex of each
section. Two guides, smooth guided sections, general guides on explicit frames and rational guides remain open.

**Model and Studio.** `copyLoftGuide` keeps the existing encoding of a single quadratic or cubic Bezier span. Other
polynomial curves copy degree, knots and controls as `nurbs`. Arrays are independent snapshots. Loft uses height
sections for a nurbs guide, sorted along the sketches' common normal. Existing Bezier guides keep their framed path.
The HUD states the vertex condition. Chat documents the same guide fields. Raw height sections refer to sketches on
one common plane; the HUD carries picked sketches onto that plane.

**A kernel error found in the WIP.** Its section interpolation used parameter λ while height used Gz(λ). A taper
therefore changed with the guide's height parameterization. The failing independent frustum oracle reported:
`volume 2.7333333333333347 != 2.3333333333333335`. Rulings now use normalized height
h(λ) = (Gz(λ) − Gz(0)) / (Gz(1) − Gz(0)), in both the control net and mass integration. Its basis coefficients are
the normalized control heights. Each slice is the corresponding ruled slice translated by the guide minus its chord.
The moment integrands, including dz, have degree at most 5p−1. The Gauss rule now uses
max(2p + 2, ceil(5p / 2)) points per knot interval: 13 at degree 5, where 12 did not cover degree 24.

**Independent oracles.**

## D289 — Open fillets can run past a single polynomial Bezier face end (2026-10-28)

**Problem.** On the quintic guided square loft used below, the plane and its neighbouring curved side meet along
an open spatial curve. The rolling ball reached the body's end, but its solve surface stopped at the polynomial
face's knot domain. A radius 0.5 face fillet failed with `CONTACT_LEAVES_FACE` near `(0, 0, 0)`.

**Decision.** For the open-chain solve only, carry a degree 2–5, single clamped polynomial Bezier direction one
quarter of its parameter range past each end. Two de Casteljau splits compute the controls of exactly the same
polynomial on the wider interval; the knots move with them. Equal weights along that direction are required.
Closed, multi-span and rational directions keep their existing treatment. The existing linear run and cylinder
whole-turn paths remain. The body's source surfaces and trim loops are not replaced. Inside-trim allowance uses
the original face domain, so widening the solve domain does not widen it. Contact/section fit tolerances and the
4096-station ceiling are unchanged. Helpers live at module scope, with no new loop closures or dependencies.

**Independent expectation.** A 20×20 square translated along
`C(t) = (20t²(1−t)²(1−2t), 0, 20t)`, 0≤t≤1, has volume 8000. Its plane/curved-side corner is square. The round
removes `r²(1−π/4) L`; the integrated signed-curvature term vanishes because both end tangents are vertical, and
the end planes are normal to those tangents. Simpson integration of
`sqrt(400 + (40t−240t²+400t³−200t⁴)²)` gives `L = 20.06333624702397` (4096/16384/65536 intervals agree at the
shown precision). At r=0.5, expected volume is `7998.923592798254`, kernel output `7998.923592765548`.
This expectation does not use kernel surface evaluation, fitted fillet controls or mass quadrature. The tests
also cover either face order, r=0.25, native save/open, Model/API names and signatures, and Studio command admission.

**Research boundary.** A scratch prototype that extended all polynomial spans preserved sampled source points
within `9e-15`, but the multi-span fillet failed `APPROX_TOLERANCE_NOT_MET` at 4096 stations. It is not adopted.
A direct ball tool on the non-adjacent quintic pair (over a smaller round) also succeeded in scratch, but the public
feature still refuses that pair: a general, bounded corner-replacement contract and guide construction are not
implemented. This decision does not close free-form face fillets as a whole or roadmap 07.

**First failures preserved.** The new native-codec test initially passed a document where `saveCadPart` requires
an evaluated snapshot: `error: 'malformed JSON'`, `code: 'FORMAT'`. It now follows the existing snapshot API.
Model and browser save/open comparisons first found `+ 0` / `- -0` in computed face signatures. They now compare
against JSON-normalised saved data; authored face names, radius and geometry checks remain. Kernel lint first
reported `src/blend/polynomial-run.ts: loop-spread 0 → 2`; explicit three-coordinate copies remove both patterns.

**Review corrections.** A small offset knot domain (`[1, 1+5*EPSILON]`) rounds the requested quarter-domain
extension. Control computation now uses the actual represented new knots; the old ideal factors changed the endpoint
by about 0.0357. A regression checks the original polynomial on that domain. A second regression covers a valid
surface at the 1e6 geometry-coordinate boundary: an extrapolated control outside the existing limit makes the helper
keep the original surface rather than causing `Coordinates must be finite and within 1e6 mm`. Unrepresentable end
margins are also skipped. An independent read-only review found no further actionable defect after these fixes.

**Verification.** Node 22.19.0, heavy gate, serial runs on the final source:
- Kernel build and whole-source lint pass. Whole suite: 1974 total, 1968 pass, 0 fail, 6 existing skips. Six new
  polynomial tests include the independent volume, codec, original-parameter preservation and domain/range guards.
- Model: tsc and the new test's lint pass; whole suite 1718/1718. Studio: tsc and whole suite 352/352.
- Real desktop Chrome/WebGPU, 1440×900 DPR1: an authored quintic loft fixture is opened; one face is selected by the
  existing named-face test hook and the visible second face by Shift-click. Face fillet r0.5 previews and applies;
  named faces and signatures are stored. Visible volume is 7999, Undo restores 8000, Redo and Save/Open restore the
  accepted node and 7999. The rounded front corner is visible in the saved screenshot. This is synthetic browser
  execution, not person-input acceptance. Only this flow and its startup prerequisite ran.
- Agent tools/refusals checks pass without regeneration. Full docs pass: 67 pages, 50 shots, 829 labels. The first

## D291 — Replace a bounded polynomial corner strip with a larger round (2026-10-28)

**Problem and scope.** D289's adjacent quintic round worked, but r0.5 across its existing r0.25 round still returned
`FACE_FILLET_FACE`. The new path handles one planar face and one polynomial translational face, one face piece each,
a convex square corner, an open regular guide, and exactly two planar end caps normal to its end tangents. The
curved chart is linear across and has one clamped polynomial span of degree2–5 along the guide. Existing analytic
corner restoration keeps priority. This does not close general free-form face fillets.

**Exact admission.** The helper recognises planarity from all represented poles and proves parameter-normal
orientation for regular polynomial translational charts. This includes the quintic fixture's planar side that
`faceGeometry` currently classifies as `other`; the global classifier is unchanged. Row differences must be the
same translation, parallel to the plane normal, with common positive weights. The projected intersection row is
exactly a stored endpoint row, so its guide is copied without another rounding. Derivative-pole projection proves
regular monotone progress. Exact Bernstein half-space signs keep the guide from re-entering either end cap.
Input and result must be closed solid bodies.

**Replacement proof boundary.** The old bridge must be one connected hole-free disk strip: Euler1, one boundary,
no branching/seam edge, and exactly one chain per selected side/end cap in cyclic side-cap-side-cap order. The
rolling ball starts with one face on each side; its returned non-deduplicated side list must still have length2.
Complete, conservative Boolean provenance must exclude every old bridge face. New faces must come only from the
tool's round faces and form the same strip against the selected sides/caps. Unrelated faces must each retain one
singleton source, the same surface/sense/name and exact oriented curve/pcurve trim correspondence. A positive
volume change above the existing body-relative floor and the kernel's strict checks are also required. These
checks retain the kernel's sampling and fit limits; they are not a global mathematical solid certificate.

**Provenance implementation.** WIP `37da7011f` adds an internal traced entrypoint; public options, package entrypoint
and B-rep JSON are unchanged. A request-local WeakMap tracks original operand+face IDs through pieces, merging and
cylinder seam splitting. Merged clusters retain a conservative source union. Every new Piece must inherit a receipt
explicitly; missing data is incomplete. Final body/shell/face IDs are checked against build order. Only the final
accepted result's receipt is returned. Source presence does not prove positive area contribution; source absence
is the conservative removal check. Tests cover identical A/B IDs, split/reversed sources, plane/cylinder merging,
freeze settings, cavity shells, empty results and an existing tangent fixture. They do not instrument a real
freeze-fallback/rejudge branch count.

**Protected representatives.** The first exact-trim attempt refused the fixture because one shared representative
x moved19.999999999999957→19.999999999999915 while surface/curve/knots/pcurves were identical. Before any restoration,
raw strict validity and complete sources are required. Unique cyclic curve correspondence builds global bijective
edge/vertex ID maps. Exact squared distance must fit the minimum of source tolerance, result tolerance and the
existing scale-aware linear limit. Only those proven corresponding representative coordinates are copied from the
source into new vertex records; result IDs/tolerances stay intact. Both operands/raw result remain unchanged. Full
strict surface/trim/vertex checks, strip checks and strict result validity run again. No tolerance is increased.

**Evidence so far.** WIP `f6e265886`: build/lint, focused kernel19/19, Model3/3 and desktop Chrome/WebGPU pass. The
independent oracle is D289's swept-square corner: `8000−r²(1−π/4)*20.06333624702397`; expected r0.5 volume
`7998.923592798254`. Face pick order, native/API Save/Open, source immutability, exact protected coordinates,
equal/smaller-round refusal, cap holes and sheet metadata are covered. Real Studio uses the existing named-face
hook for the first pick and Shift-click for the visible second: preview/apply, Undo/Redo and Save/Open pass; visible
volume7999, Undo to the smaller round8000. This is synthetic browser execution, not person-input acceptance.

**First failures.** Initial kernel candidate:18 total,14 pass/4 fail with `FACE_FILLET_FACE` and `assert.ok(output)`:
the exact plane check was gated on the narrower global classifier. After coefficient admission:19 total,16 pass/
3 fail with `[FACE_FILLET_NOT_CLEAR] an unrelated face or its oriented trim changed during polynomial corner
replacement`. Inspection found the representative drift above. The protected-coordinate restoration makes19/19
pass. The Model replacement baseline similarly began2 pass/1 `FACE_FILLET_FACE` failure, then passed3/3.

**Final verification.** The serial Node22 window on the combined WIP source at `cf3d02151` passes kernel build,
whole kernel lint and1987 tests:1981 pass,0 fail,6 existing skips. Model tsc, changed-file lint and1729/1729 pass;
Studio tsc and352/352 pass. The earlier focused desktop Chrome/WebGPU startup+replacement flow used the same
unchanged replacement source; its saved reopened image was inspected. Full browser, WebGL2/mobile/GPU, RB/fuzz
and release were not repeated. Final generated-tools/refusals and whole docs results are recorded with D292.

**Remaining.** General pairs, concave corners, multiple pieces per support, rational/multi-span guides, cap/side
holes, other contacted faces, ambiguous provenance and protected reparameterisation remain refused. No feature

## D292 — Read bounded static TrueType data from the selected font originals (2026-10-28)

**Decision.** `engine/font/trueType.ts` reads an independent copied Uint8Array snapshot and returns metrics plus one
Unicode scalar's glyph ID, advance, bearing and unhinted on/off quadratic contour points in font design units.
`copyBytes` and every glyph query return independent data. Metrics are frozen. The existing BarocssError class
carries local TTF codes and `details.source='true-type'`. The package export map is unchanged; its existing wildcard
exposes this engine module's six type declarations and two functions. No document schema or UI is changed.

**Profile.** One static sfnt with head/maxp/hhea/hmtx/cmap4-or12/short-or-long-loca/glyf; format12 has priority.

plus nonzero offset needs an explicit offset policy. Instructions are bounded and skipped. No missing-glyph
substitution occurs; mapped space can remain empty. WOFF/CFF/TTC/variable fonts, point attachment, ROUND_XY_TO_GRID,
USE_MY_METRICS, conflicting/reserved flags, malformed extents, cycles and budget excess are explicitly refused.

loca, delta/repeat, transform, snapshot, malformed/cycle/budget fixtures cover parser boundaries. No source or font

## D293 — Carry original byte assets through the existing blob paths (2026-10-28)

**Decision.** Add `Uint8Array`/`u8` to BlobArray, the blob store and the current BCADPACK codec. Byte chunks use
width 1 and bounded integer counts. Base64, worker data, recovery and container Save/Open reuse the existing
paths. Container version stays 1; document schema handling is unchanged. No top-level font registry, dtype hash namespace,
runtime dependency or WASM is added. Existing raw-byte content addressing is unchanged.

**Font ownership.** `engine/font/source.ts` admits only the explicit descriptor `{blob,filename,source?,license?}`.
`fontFromBytes` copies and validates input bytes and metadata before its first await, stores the original bytes,
then checks the stored byte view. `readFontSource` always reads an explicit Uint8Array view, even when a same-byte
cache entry has another array class; the TrueType reader makes its own snapshot. Metadata is preserved as
supplied. It does not establish a license or glyph coverage.

**References.** `fontRefs` and `blobRefs` share traversal of nodes, instances, pending parts and open proposals.
The precise prepared `run_command`/`text` font-JSON boundary is collected through existing nested apply_ops/propose
paths. JSON is bounded to 512KiB in UTF-8; malformed values are skipped without breaking collection. This is
conservative asset retention, not text admission. Accepted/rejected proposals do not retain assets alone. Undo
documents, base64/recovery and native Save/Open keep referenced font bytes. Templates explicitly refuse such
documents because their current path cannot carry fonts; existing raw stored template entries are preserved.

**Evidence.** Checkpoint `0f836e8f2` includes focused Model 63/63 and Studio 15/15 for the integrated text boundary.
Synthetic u8 chunk tests exercise the codec without claiming a font workflow. Actual font workflow evidence is
recorded in D295. The initial upload fixture path failed with 1 pass/2 fail:

## D294 — Build bounded line profiles from original TrueType quadratics (2026-10-28)

**Decision.** `engine/font/profiles.ts` converts a scalar run using explicit em size, tracking and chord tolerance.
The original input string and font stay authoritative. Implied on-curve points and recursive quadratic subdivision
produce native line profiles; the bound includes arithmetic uncertainty. Tolerance is never enlarged. Size means
em height in mm, not ink bounds; tracking is added between scalars only. Browser glyph rendering is not used.

**Topology and limits.** Separation/control-hull checks precede the kernel nonzero-fill arrangement. Each glyph
occurrence returns components with their own outer boundary and holes, so an island inside a hole survives as a
separate component. Profiles are not globally unioned here. The run admits at most 256 printable Unicode scalars,
4096 contours, 65536 raw points per glyph, 4096 flattened glyph segments, 8192 run segments, 1048576 pair-work steps
and 20 subdivision levels. Native loops are bounded to 1024 segments and edges at least 1e-4 mm; coordinates stay
within 10000 mm. Tolerance must be finite, at least 1e-7 mm and no greater than size/8. Unsupported topology,
uncertain boundary proximity and excess work are typed refusals, not permission to relax tolerance.

## D296 — Bound text emboss/engrave to one supported +Z cap (2026-10-28)

**Decision.** Add native `profile-relief` over existing component sketches, and Model `kind:'text-relief'` over the
original scalar/font source. The authored modifier stores parent, exactly one exact unmerged faces name,
text/FontSource/em size/flatness/tracking, world-XY baseline at, positive depth, mode and existing NodeExtras/sigs.
There is no plane, copied top Z, Made authority, font registry, schema/container version bump or runtime dependency.
The default font is still absent. Existing standalone Text expansion, IDs and disconnected-body semantics stay
separate; relief requires one physical solid before and after.

**Native support and checks.** One native line-only upright slab with a closed strict-valid B-rep is admitted.
The selected exact face must be a +Z plane at its current top. Its outer/inner oriented loops define F; the actual
slab material including holes/concavities defines M. For every filled component C, exact finite-polygon checks
require C minus M and C minus F empty. Full polygons are used, not a bounding box or only vertex containment.
Requested font flatness is additional clearance above the existing scale-aware native linear policy; the exact
sum is rounded upward. Native tolerance is not enlarged. Pair separation accounts for both component bounds.
Overlapping/touching/near components and partial/floating support are refused before any temporary operation.

Emboss requires a represented positive raised height and basal seat. Engrave depth stays below the slab thickness
and leaves a bottom web above native linear policy. All levels and coordinates must be representable and bounded.
Each component needs full positive basal overlap and the intended signed area-times-represented-depth change.
Direct emboss slabs or one batched 2D engraving difference commit only after one closed physical result and strict checks. Rational slab/straight-B-rep
volume agreement and bounded reported mass error are audited; this is not full set equivalence or a universal
geometry certificate. A caller forcing mutation through readonly output types is not protected by runtime freezing.
The split-coplanar-cap regression exercises the internal helper, not an independently authored public native document.

**Remove duplicate work without raising limits.** Exact orientation reuses the existing homogeneous predicate and
request-local point cache. Dyadic area sums integer crosses at one common power-of-two denominator and calls rat
once. Directed-endpoint multisets provide a linear boundary fast path, with exact split/merge coverage fallback.
Emboss constructs supported slabs without Boolean calls; engrave performs one batched planar difference. Exact
oriented frontier equality checks the complete source-minus-component boundary, including counters; a dyadic 3D
audit checks the straight B-rep volume. Existing numeric policies and work/count/bit limits stay unchanged.

**Model and consumers.** The shared original-font/profile pipeline retains component-local holes. Relief emits one
default-XY/Z0 sketch per translated component and one final profile-relief with clearance=tolerance and individual
expect, within 64-component/512-native-feature and existing profile/coordinate budgets. Generated sketch IDs map to
the authored modifier only in the proper node context, with exact authored IDs first. A missing selected signature
is structurally readable but native expansion refuses BAD_REFERENCE; editor/API capture before evaluation.
Reference signatures identify the authored selected face, not fixed geometry: an ordinary source-height edit can
track its new top. Parent/uses/output/suppression/active-orphan, flatten/remap, current reader, source refs/proposals,
worker/recovery/container and parameter paths consume the recipe. Text/font remain opaque during remapping.
